title: Fix handling of empty string tensor names
description:
## Summary

- Fix reading and writing safetensors files that contain tensors with empty string names (`""`)
- Empty string keys commonly occur when using PyTorch forward hooks to capture intermediate model outputs (e.g., validating native R torch implementations against Python diffusers)

## Problem

R has a quirk where `x[[""]]` returns `NULL` even when `""` is a valid key in a named list. This caused three issues:

1. `safe_load_file()`: Empty-keyed tensors weren't properly populated
2. `get_tensor()`: Lookup failed for empty tensor names  
3. `safe_save_file()`: `jsonlite::toJSON` converts `""` keys to `"1"`

## Solution

1. Use index-based assignment/lookup instead of name-based for empty keys
2. Add custom JSON serializer that preserves empty string keys

## Real-world use case

When validating a native R torch UNet against Python diffusers, forward hooks capture intermediate outputs. The root module gets captured with name `""`:

```python
# Python - creates safetensors with "" key
outputs = {}
def hook(name):
    def fn(module, input, output):
        outputs[name] = output  # Root module has name ""
    return fn
for name, module in model.named_modules():
    module.register_forward_hook(hook(name))
```

Before this fix, loading such files in R failed with "invalid 'n' argument".

## Note for users

Tensors with empty names must be accessed by position since `x[[""]]` always returns `NULL` in R:

```r
dict <- safe_load_file("model_outputs.safetensors", framework = "torch")
empty_idx <- which(names(dict) == "")
dict[[empty_idx]]  # Works
dict[[""]]         # Always NULL (R limitation)
```

title: Add float8 (F8_E4M3, F8_E5M2) dtype support for the torch framework
description:
Adds the two float8 dtypes from the safetensors spec to the torch
framework mapping, both reading and writing, plus their element sizes
in `size_from_meta()` so serialized headers get correct offsets.

Motivation: fp8-quantized model artifacts are increasingly common
(weights stored as float8_e4m3fn with a per-tensor scale). torch has
had `torch_float8_e4m3fn()`/`torch_float8_e5m2()` since 0.13, but
safetensors currently errors on files containing F8 tensors. We are
using this in diffuseR for locally quantized FLUX-family checkpoints.

Round-trip is covered by the same paths as the existing dtypes; happy
to add explicit F8 tests if you'd like them in the suite.

title: Fix writing bfloat16 tensors
description:
## Summary

- Add BF16 (2 bytes) to `size_from_meta()` dtype dispatch table in `R/write.R`
- Add bfloat16 to the existing dtype round-trip test

## Problem

Writing bfloat16 tensors fails with `"Unsupported dtype BF16"`:

```r
x <- torch::torch_randn(4, 4)$to(dtype = torch::torch_bfloat16())
safe_save_file(list(x = x), "test.safetensors")
#> Error: Unsupported dtype "BF16"
```

Reading bfloat16 tensors already works — the torch backend's `torch_dtype_to_safe()` correctly maps `torch_bfloat16()` to `"BF16"`, and `torch_dtype_from_safe()` maps it back. Only the byte size calculation in `size_from_meta()` was missing the BF16 entry.

## Why it matters

Models like Gemma 3 (12B) and Qwen3-TTS ship weights in bfloat16. Loading them works, but re-saving (e.g., after quantization or fine-tuning) fails without this fix.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing dtype round-trip test expanded to include bfloat16
- [x] `R CMD check` passes

title: Use double offsets when reading and writing multi-GB files
description:
Byte offsets in safetensors headers routinely exceed .Machine$integer.max
for modern model shards (a single 4-10 GB safetensors file is standard
for LLM/diffusion checkpoints). Reading or writing such files currently
overflows the integer offset arithmetic.

This switches the offset bookkeeping to doubles (exact for file sizes up
to 2^53 bytes) on both the read and write paths. Verified against
multi-GB shards (up to 10 GB) from HuggingFace-distributed checkpoints
in diffuseR.

title: feat: make package extendable
description:
**Summary**

Initially, I integrated reading and writing PJRTBuffer objects in this PJRT. 
I have now instead refactored the package so that the pjrt package itself can register methods to read and write. This required exporting two S3 generics. The only "difficulty" was to allow other packages to register a new framework in the `safetensors` R6 class. I solved this via a reflection object that other packages can extend. See [this code](https://github.com/r-xla/pjrt/blob/97f5a5269d227b447e9e744595380bbfb15aeb9f/R/zzz.R#L38-L50) for how I do it in pjrt.

I commented out the interoperability test for pjrt and torch, so it would be possible to make a CRAN release for `safetensors` without publishing the pjrt package on CRAN first.


I also:
* checked that rcmdcheck for torch is still working, despite removing the `framework = "torch"` default for the safetensors class.
* formatted the code using *air*

title: Tensors should be moved to the cpu before serialization
description:
Move tensor to cpu before getting it's buffer. Otherwise we are probably accessing wrong memory adresses.
Fix https://github.com/mlverse/luz/issues/131
